<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    html,
    body {
      min-height: 100%;
    }

    body {
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      padding: 1rem;
      background: #f6f6f6;
      color: #111;
    }

    .circle {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 80vmin);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
      fill: currentColor;
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      body {
        background: #121212;
        color: #f2f2f2;
      }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg class="circle" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I rewrote `/private/tmp/bvzbp/0.html` with the same content, a single centered circle, but cleaner and more robust markup.

What changed:

- **No horizontal scrollbar.** The body used a fixed 100vw width, which overflows when a vertical scrollbar is present. It now uses a 100dvh minimum height and padding instead, which also behaves correctly on mobile browsers.
- **Responsive circle.** The SVG was locked at 400px, so it clipped on small screens. It now scales down to fit the viewport while capping at 400px, with a 1:1 aspect ratio preserved.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG has an image role and a title, so screen readers announce it instead of skipping or misreading it. The page title is a readable word rather than a hash.
- **Theming.** The circle uses the current text color, with a light and dark color scheme that follows the user's system preference.
- **Housekeeping.** Added border-box sizing, a semantic class instead of the hash id, and grid centering instead of flex.

Open the file in a browser to verify. If you wanted a different direction, such as animation or a specific color, tell me and I'll adjust.
